title: Fixing the Amount Open to Challenge on a Car Rental Recharge
content:
What is open to challenge on the damage recharged is read from the damage lines the ledger carries and from
the reviews standing against the rental. This is the basis across the Car Rental Rate Classes.

**Where the ledger carries more than one damage recharge on the rental**, the amount open to challenge is
the largest single damage recharge the ledger carries.

**Where a review already stands declined against the rental**, the amount open to challenge is the whole of
what the ledger carries as recharged damage less the rate class's damage administration charge, and never
less than nothing. The administration charge taken off is the figure published by the rate class booked.

**Where neither holds of a rental**, nothing under this head changes the amount open to challenge.

## Which case is reached first

The two cases are taken in the order they stand. A rental carrying three damage recharges and also a
declined review is answered by the first: the amount open to challenge is the largest of the three, and no
administration charge is taken off.

More than one damage recharge means two or more damage lines standing on that rental's ledger. A rental
carrying a single damage line does not reach the first case, whatever the size of the line.

## Three ledgers worked through

A rental whose ledger carries damage recharges of 430 USD, 980 USD and 275 USD: the amount open to challenge
is 980 USD. A rental carrying a single damage recharge of 300 USD against which a review already stands
declined, on a class whose damage administration charge is 125 USD: the amount open to challenge is 175 USD.
Were that single recharge 95 USD on the same class, the subtraction would fall below nothing and the amount
open to challenge would be nothing.
